newsitem.title: USA: Thrift industry praises supervisor nominee Seidman.
newsitem.headline: Thrift industry praises supervisor nominee Seidman.

text.p: Representatives of the U.S. thrift industry praised the Clinton Administration's announced nominee to head the Office of Thrift Supervision, Ellen Seidman.
The White House said Wednesday it intended to nominate Seidman, currently special assistant to the president for economic policy on the National Economic Council.
"I'm very enthusiastic," said Robert Davis, director of government relations for a leading thrift trade group, America's Community bankers.
"She is one who is really making things work behind the scenes," Davis said. "She's very, very savy."
Seidman worked at Federal National Mortgage Association before joining the Clinton team and had previous stints at the departments of Transportation and Treasury.

Treasury Secretary Robert Rubin also praised the nomination. Seidman "has made great contributions to the Administration's economic achievments at the NEC and is well-suited to lead OTS at a time when the financial services sector of the economy is undergoing rapid change," Rubin said in a statement.
Seidman received an MBA from George Washington University and a law degree from Georgetown University.
Thrift industry officials said Seidman was a key player on legislation last year to bail out the Savings Insurance Fund and on an earlier public-private housing initiative.
If approved by the Senate, Seidman might find herself quickly battling for the survival of the Office of Thrift Supervision.
A General Accounting Office report last November suggested merging the thrift office with the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency and the Federal Deposit Insurance Corp.

Such efforts may get renewed attention as Congress begins to debate financial sector reform. Two bills proposed in the House would merge the charters under which banks and thrifts operate, possibly obviating the need for a separate thrift regulator.
